data.body_html:
Choosing between the Astondoa 40 and the Fairline Targa 12m for your Marbella boat charter? Both are excellent vessels departing from Puerto Banús, but they cater to slightly different preferences. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is a sporty open cruiser available at fixed Tier A pricing (€749/2h to €2,299/8h), while the Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) offers a more enclosed cockpit and flexible pricing on request. This guide breaks down their specs, strengths, and ideal use cases for your day on the Costa del Sol.

Boat Specifications at a Glance

Here is a quick comparison of the key numbers for both vessels:

FeatureAstondoa 40Fairline Targa 12m
Length12.5 m12 m
Max Passengers910
Departure PointPuerto BanúsPuerto Banús
Pricing€749/2h – €2,299/8h (Tier A)On request (WhatsApp)
InclusionsSkipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, VATSkipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, VAT

Design and Onboard Experience

The Astondoa 40 is a sleek, open-cruiser with a spacious sun pad aft and a large forward seating area. Its open layout is perfect for sunbathing and socialising, with a bimini top for shade. The Fairline Targa 12m features a more enclosed cockpit with a hardtop and roll-back sunroof, offering better protection from the sun or wind. Both have a small cabin below deck for changing and a compact galley. If you prefer an airy, sun-drenched deck, go for the Astondoa; if you want more shelter, the Fairline is ideal.

Passenger Capacity and Group Dynamics

The Astondoa 40 takes up to 9 guests, while the Fairline Targa 12m can carry 10. For a group of 8-9 friends, either boat works. The Astondoa's open cockpit encourages mingling, while the Fairline's L-shaped seating in the cockpit offers a more intimate dining setup. Both have a forward sun pad for lounging. For larger groups, consider our Mangusta 80 (12 pax).

Pricing and Value

The Astondoa 40 is priced transparently at €749 for 2 hours, €1,199 for 4 hours, €1,599 for 6 hours, and €2,299 for 8 hours (all inclusive). The Fairline Targa 12m requires a custom quote via WhatsApp – this gives flexibility for bespoke itineraries or longer charters. If you prefer instant booking with a fixed price, the Astondoa is the straightforward choice. For tailored trips, the Fairline can be negotiated.

Best Destinations from Puerto Banús

Both boats are ideal for exploring the Marbella coastline. Popular stops include Cala del Faro (a quiet cove 20 minutes east), Cabopino (30 minutes west, with its dunes and chiringuitos), or Estepona (45 minutes west, for the old town). Your skipper will recommend the best route based on sea conditions and your preferences. The Astondoa's shallow draft (approx. 1m) allows closer anchoring near beaches.

Performance and Handling

Both boats are powered by twin inboard diesel engines (typically Volvo Penta). The Astondoa 40 cruises at 20-25 knots with a top speed around 30 knots. The Fairline Targa 12m is similarly capable, offering a comfortable cruising speed of 22-26 knots. Fuel is included in both charters, so you can enjoy the ride without worrying about costs. Stability is excellent on both, thanks to their deep-V hulls.

Which One Should You Choose?

Choose the Astondoa 40 if you want a sporty, open-boat experience with fixed pricing and a maximum of 9 guests. It is perfect for a lively day of sun, swimming, and socialising. Choose the Fairline Targa 12m if you need space for 10 passengers or prefer a more sheltered cockpit, and you are open to discussing a custom price. Both deliver the quintessential Marbella charter experience from Puerto Banús. For more options, browse our full fleet of boats in Marbella.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which boat is bigger, the Astondoa 40 or Fairline Targa 12m?

The Astondoa 40 measures 12.5m, while the Fairline Targa 12m is 12m. The difference is minimal, but the Astondoa is slightly longer. However, the Fairline Targa 12m has a more enclosed cockpit and can carry up to 10 passengers, compared to the Astondoa's 9.

How much does it cost to charter the Astondoa 40 vs Fairline Targa 12m?

The Astondoa 40 is part of our Tier A pricing: €749 for 2 hours, €2,299 for 8 hours. The Fairline Targa 12m has pricing on request; contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote based on your itinerary and duration.

Which boat is better for a party or group outing in Marbella?

The Fairline Targa 12m can accommodate up to 10 passengers, one more than the Astondoa 40's 9. The Fairline also offers a more sheltered cockpit, which can be preferable for longer trips. For a lively but intimate party, the Astondoa 40's open layout is excellent for sunbathing and socialising.

Can I take both boats to Cala del Faro or Cabopino?

Yes, both the Astondoa 40 and Fairline Targa 12m are well-suited for day trips to Cala del Faro, Cabopino beach, or even Estepona. Their lengths (12-12.5m) allow easy anchoring in calm coves. Your skipper will handle navigation and mooring.

What is included in the charter price for these boats?

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21% VAT). No hidden extras – just show up and enjoy.

Which boat is faster, the Astondoa 40 or Fairline Targa 12m?

Both are planing hulls with similar power-to-weight ratios. The Astondoa 40 typically cruises at 20-25 knots, while the Fairline Targa 12m is also capable of similar speeds. Exact performance depends on sea conditions and load.

Do I need a boating licence to charter these boats?

No. Both boats come with a licensed skipper who handles all navigation. You can relax and enjoy the trip without any licence or experience.

How do I book the Fairline Targa 12m if pricing is on request?

Simply send us a WhatsApp message with your desired date, duration, and number of guests. We'll respond with a personalised quote within hours. For the Astondoa 40, you can book directly online via our Tier A pricing.
